what: The numeric price column cannot be shown formatted or sorted another documented way, so the admin table shows 79.9 and the builder only renamed the header to 'Price (EUR)' to fit it.
why: The DataColumn schema has formatValue and sort settings, but the builder found no documented way to format a numeric column value (R1-1 and R6-4 remain open).
workaround: Kept the numeric column with a shorter label and a width; formatting left open.
note: DataColumn formatValue is listed (line 38) but not what it does; GAPS R12-3 shows generated numeric columns only get a localized number, no currency. Say formatValue is locale number formatting only; for a currency use a unit in the label or a custom visual element with the shared Price component.

what: Creating a transfer object with a mapping auto-creates the mapped members (lineTotal, total and so on), so hand-made derived members with the same names gave 'not unique' and binding errors on validation.
why: Behaviour of mapped transfer objects not described where the builder looked; the same lesson was learned in R7 (R7-14) and repeated.
workaround: Deleted the duplicated hand-made members and kept the auto-created ones; validation passed.
proposed_target: catalog/best-practices/model/unmapped-transfer-dto.md or a mapped-transfer-object page: mapping creates members
note: Nothing in the catalog says a transfer object with a mapping auto-creates the mapped members, so a hand-made derived member of the same name is "not unique" (repeat of R7-14). Add one sentence: reuse the generated member, name derived members differently.

what: Validator warnings appeared after the Customer product access changed: 'Columns are not defined for the viewable table' and 'Principal of actor Customer should not have relations and operations'.
why: Not explained by the builder; the warnings were noted in the CLI output and not acted on.
note: Only warnings noted in CLI output, no failed behaviour and no claim about the catalog; nothing to validate.

what: An OperationForm placed directly in a view fails UI validation (ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition, NamedElementHaveToBeInApplication); the operation must sit in an ActionGroup, and the catalog says direct placement works.
why: The catalog section on operation wiring says OperationForm inside View or Form works; the transformation rejects it. The openspec sweep already lists ActionGroup-wrapped OperationForms as an open item (FR-033). Even inside an ActionGroup, the validator still reported action container errors after the wrap (session:L2494).
workaround: Moved both operations into an ActionGroup named actions, set label Actions and featuredActions=1; for checkout the action container errors cleared only after it became void with generateActionsHook=true (validation passed, session:L2522).
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/model/ui-authoring-guide.md section 10 (OperationForm in ActionGroup is required; constraints on action container)
note: ui-authoring-guide lines 131 and 190 say OperationForm can sit directly in a View/Form; the session shows the transformation rejects it and needs an ActionGroup. Already listed as open in judo-doc-problems (ActionGroup-wrapped OperationForms). Change the text: operation buttons go inside a ui:ActionGroup.

what: After generate or build, target/judo-cli.jar disappeared, so every CLI call failed with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root was run again.
why: generate and build do not recreate the CLI jar; only generate-root (or the validate goal) copies it. Known from earlier rounds (R7-7, S01).
workaround: Helper script .scratch/ensure-cli.sh runs generate-root when the jar is missing; used before every CLI step.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/model/judo-cli.md (generate and build do not restore the jar)
note: judo-cli.md line 15 says ./judo.sh build downloads target/judo-cli.jar; GAPS S01-2 shows neither build nor generate-root created it first time, and the session shows it missing after generate/build until generate-root ran again. State: restore with ./judo.sh generate-root (or mvn -DgenerateRoot validate) and check the jar exists before CLI calls.

what: The builder said the kb had no entry for the generated DAO method names, error handler and customization constants; the DAO names were read from the generated SDK instead.
why: Claim is unverified: data-access-guide.md exists in the catalog and the builder read it at session:L2364 for another question. The kb-first search was not run for these names.
workaround: Read generated SDK and frontend source directly.
note: data-access-guide.md covers DAO query/create methods and the builder read it at L2364; the kb-first search was not run for these names. Retrieval problem, not a catalog gap.

what: No catalog text found by the builder on whether a custom operation rolls back on error; the builder proved it with a test instead (stock of the first line restored when the second line throws a ShopFault).
why: The backend docs cover rollback for interceptors and for integration test modes (AUTO_ROLLBACK) but not the runtime rule for custom operations; the builder's kb search for the rule found nothing.
workaround: Integration-style Playwright test proves the rollback of stock, cart and order.
note: custom-operations.md only has test transaction modes (AUTO_ROLLBACK); no runtime rule. Builder proved by test that an exception in a custom operation rolls back all its writes. Add that line (mark verify against the dispatcher).

what: The documented menu reorder example sorts by item ids such as dashboard, but generated menu ids are long model ids, so the example cannot be used as written.
why: The catalog example does not show the real id format of generated menu items.
workaround: Sorted the menu by item title (Products, Cart, My orders, My profile, My addresses) in registerShellHooks.ts; test checks the five labels.
note: The Reordering Menu Items example (line 340) orders by ids like dashboard and entities; generated menu item ids are long model ids. Change the example to match on a suffix or the real id format.

what: A 0..1 relation query returns Optional<Product>, while a 1..1 relation query returns the entity; the first build failed with a type mismatch because the builder assumed Optional.
why: The kb says single-valued relation queries return the entity but does not separate optional (0..1) from mandatory (1..1) relations.
workaround: Used the entity directly for the 1..1 cart line product relation (RemoveProductCustomImplementation.java).
note: data-access-guide (lines 289-304) says single-valued relation queries return the entity directly; the generated SDK returns Optional<T> for 0..1 (SalesOrderLineDao shows Optional types). Split the rule: 0..1 returns Optional, 1..1 returns the entity.

what: The per-relation createHistory method did not exist until the relation had createable=true, which the builder only found after a failed build.
why: relation-based-entity-creation.md states the createable rule in one sentence that the builder missed on first read.
workaround: Set createable=true on SalesOrder.history in the model, then the generated create method appeared.
note: The page says the create method exists only if the relation allows creation but never names the createable=true attribute. Add: set createable=true on the relation or createX is not generated.

what: No documented way to backdate or seed an old order in a running-app Playwright test, so the 30-day cut-off itself is untested.
why: Order timestamps are set only by checkout; the initializer has no documented trigger; the kb fixture examples are for Java integration tests, not the running app.
workaround: Test checks that today's order is in the 30-day list and in All orders; the cut-off is left untested and logged.
proposed_target: catalog/best-practices/backend/init-data-seeding.md (seed or backdate rows for running-app tests)
note: No page covers seeding or backdating rows for a running-app Playwright test (init-data-seeding and runtime-fixture pages cover Java tests only). Add the route used (SQL via psql or a test-only operation).

what: create -t ActionGroup without a parent was refused (Cannot create ActionGroup in Model); the group must be created with --ns of the view, then operations are relocated into it.
why: The ui-authoring-guide says an OperationForm inside a view works, but gives no CLI recipe for the ActionGroup.
workaround: create -t ActionGroup -n actions --ns <view>, then relocate each operation into it.
note: No CLI recipe for creating an ActionGroup (create -t ActionGroup needs --ns of the view; operations are then moved in). Add it next to the ActionGroup row at line 191.

what: Validator warned that the principal of actor Customer should not have relations and operations; the builder did not address the warning.
why: Principal rule for actors with relations is not explained in the catalog pages the builder read.
workaround: None; warning left in place.
note: Same validator warning as c04-09, not acted on, no failed behaviour.

what: History rows show the login e-mail as the actor, not a person's name.
why: ACTOR variable gives the e-mail; no documented way to show a name in a history row was found.
workaround: Left as is and logged as open.
note: True that the ACTOR variable gives the login e-mail (platform-behavior-reference lists variables); no failure and no catalog claim being wrong. Showing a name needs a lookup in the model, a design choice.

what: The Ordered field on the admin order view showed a date picker icon although it should be read-only; a derived boolean in enabledBy greyed it out but left the picker.
why: The kb has no read-only switch for a mapped timestamp field; isReadOnly exists only for derived members.
workaround: Derived string orderedAtLabel replaces the field on both order views (sorting keeps the real timestamp); test checks a text box with no date group or picker button.
note: textWidget TEXT is the only read-only switch (string fields only, line 45). Nothing for date, number or enum fields. Add the options: show a derived (non-editable) member instead of the mapped one, or use enabledBy and accept the picker.

what: No runnable recipe in the kb for a Markdown Handlebars template rendered to PDF; the only document pipeline in the kb is the DOCX XDocReport one.
why: Catalog covers Handlebars email rendering, file store transfer and inline preview, but no Markdown to PDF step.
workaround: invoice.md.hbs rendered with Handlebars 4.2.0 (already in runtime), turned into PDF by a small Markdown renderer on PDFBox 2.0.13 (already in runtime), stored via FileStoreService, returned as FileType.
note: No recipe for Markdown plus Handlebars rendered to PDF; judo-doc-problems already records a project that migrated to it (entry about replacing the XDocReport leg). Write the pipeline page.

what: The XDocReport DOCX pipeline blueprint is still presented as a current pattern with no deprecation note, although the project lead says the pipeline is deprecated.
why: Blueprint status fields say single-project and do not mark deprecation.
workaround: Not used; a Markdown route was built instead.
note: Blueprint has no deprecation note. judo-doc-problems describes XDocReport as the legacy leg replaced by Markdown plus Handlebars, which supports the claim (the lead statement itself is unverifiable). Add a legacy note linking the replacement.

what: Platform-provided libraries (PDFBox, Handlebars, FileStoreService) do not compile in the app module until the app pom declares them; the first build failed with unresolved imports.
why: Catalog does not say that runtime-provided libraries still need a compile-time dependency in the app module.
workaround: Added pom.xml.extra-dependencies.fragment.hbs (documented fragment slot), then build -i succeeded.
note: build-process worked example (line 125) adds a runtime dependency but does not say platform-provided libraries (PDFBox, Handlebars, FileStoreService) still need compile-time dependencies in the app pom. Add that line.

what: application_hu-HU.json is not generated: the generator emits only application_en-US.json for this one-language model, while the i18n doc says every application_<locale>.json, including hu-HU, is generated from the model.
why: Catalog statement is wrong for a model with one language.
workaround: scripts/make-hu-translations.py builds the Hungarian file from the generated English file (about 190 labels translated; the rest English).
note: i18n.md lines 18-23 and 108 say application_hu-HU.json is generated; the generator emits only locales that exist in the model (one-language model gives en-US only). Add: other locale files are written by hand or by a project script and need each new key added.

what: The generated locale map in l10n-context.tsx allows only en-US, and no date-fns locale exists for Hungarian, so the language switch needs a cast and date pickers stay English.
why: i18n Adding New Languages steps copy JSON files and update the selector but do not mention the locales map.
workaround: Language switch uses the documented L10N setLocale with a cast; date formatting left English.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/i18n.md (Adding New Languages: locales map and date-fns locale)
note: Adding New Languages does not mention the generated locale map in l10n-context.tsx (en-US only) or the date-fns locale (only line 487 shows hu). Add both steps.

what: The header tracks only one AppBarExtraComponents service, while ui-hooks.md shows several AppBar components; the drawer fix and the language switch had to be merged into one component.
why: Generated HeaderContent uses a single useTrackService lookup.
workaround: AppBarExtras.tsx combines DrawerExpander and LanguageSwitch and is registered once.
note: ui-hooks.md line 46 now says the AppBar accepts exactly one extra component and a Multiple AppBar Components section (line 214) shows merging into one. Already fixed; builder read an older or skipped text.

what: The shop settings singleton has no startup seed: the model blueprint says the row is seeded by an initializer, but no startup trigger is documented, so the admin enters it once through the UI and a second row is not prevented by the model.
why: Catalog gives no trigger for init operations and no rule for singleton duplicates in the running app.
workaround: Seed test creates the settings row through the admin UI if none exists.
note: The initializer blueprint says the project calls init from a startup or deployment routine but gives no concrete trigger and no singleton duplicate guard. Add: the platform does not auto-run init (verify); call it from a deployment script and guard with a count check.

what: The CSV export custom operation threw a NullPointerException on input.getFromDate().orElse(...) when the user left the date empty, because the optional input getter returned null, not Optional.empty.
why: Custom operation input getters for optional attributes can return null; the agent-docs custom-operations page does not say this where the builder looked, and the sweep inventory (BA-042) already flagged it.
workaround: Null-guarded the getters and the status filter in ExportOrdersCustomImplementation.
note: custom-operations.md does not say that optional input getters can return null instead of Optional.empty (sweep item BA-042). Add: null-check optional input getters (verify).

what: Builder claimed a write made in a postCall interceptor on the notification refresh was not kept: the log said 'marked as read' but the database kept c_read = f.
why: Builder did not isolate the cause; catalog says postCall runs in the transaction and rolls back the write on exception, which does not explain a silent drop.
workaround: Moved the read marking to a custom operation markRead called from the page post-refresh hook (see c06-14).
note: Builder never isolated the cause of the dropped postCall write; read-tracking-postcall-interceptor.md describes the transaction rule correctly. No catalog statement to fix without a reproduction.

what: The 'Ordered' text and history times differed by two hours: the model-built string orderedAtLabel used the platform zone (UTC), while the generated history column rendered in the browser zone (CET).
why: Model expressions follow the platform defaultZoneId, the UI follows the browser; the catalog says so but gives no model-side way to show the browser zone. Container is UTC, host CET; default zone already UTC so storage needed no change.
workaround: Removed the derived string; see c06-16.
note: Time and Time Zones section (line 94) already says model expressions follow defaultZoneId, not the JVM. Add the contrast: generated UI columns render in the browser zone, so model-built strings differ by the zone offset.

what: ./judo.sh schema-upgrade fails with ProjectBuildingException because SCHEMA_DIR defaults to the model directory (project root), so the schema POM path is <root>/schema. Setting schema_dir=application makes it run, but no catalog page says schema_dir exists.
why: judo.sh derives SCHEMA_DIR from model_dir; in this layout the schema module lives under application/, and the catalog does not document schema_dir.
workaround: Ran schema_dir=application ./judo.sh schema-upgrade, and later the generate/execute route (see c07 F52 decision).
note: Confirmed from judo.sh (GAPS R12-1): SCHEMA_DIR defaults to the model dir; schema_dir env var or judo.properties line fixes layouts where schema lives under application/. grep over the catalog finds no schema_dir. Add it to the schema-upgrade row.

what: schema-upgrade runs apply (generate and execute in one step), so there is no moment to insert the hand-written backfill changeset that the catalog recommends. The catalog's schema-upgrade row does not warn about this.
why: The command table describes schema-upgrade as generate-and-apply; the backfill route needs generate, edit, then execute as separate steps.
workaround: Used judo-rdbms-schema:generate with the old model file, wrote 06_updateDataAfterIncremental by hand, then :execute.
note: build-process line 283 says schema-upgrade generates and applies in one step but does not warn that the hand-written backfill cannot be inserted. Add: for backfill use generate then judo-rdbms-schema:execute separately (route in GAPS R12-1).

what: The top-N expression form is unclear: !sort(...)!heads(5) fails in asm2query with 'Missing variable name', and !heads(p | ..., 5) validates but returns only one row at runtime. The catalog lists !heads(n) without a working top-N example.
why: The catalog documents heads and sort separately; the lambda form and its runtime behaviour are not shown.
workaround: Used filter then sort with DESC and let the table page show 5 rows.
note: model-development line 332 lists !heads(n) with no top-N example; judo-doc-problems already notes heads is under-documented. Add a validated top-N form and its runtime result once checked (verify).

what: The label of a row action must be set on the operation form element (TableOperation::<op>::<op>), not on the TableOperation. Setting label on the TableOperation or on a guessed element name failed with 'element not found' or 'label not defined'.
why: Element naming and the label location for row actions are not shown in the catalog.
workaround: Set label on ...::changePricesTableOperation::changePrices and ...::requestReturnTableOperation::requestReturn.
note: Element naming for row action labels is not shown; label belongs on the operation form element TableOperation::<op>::<op>. Add one example with the CLI update command.

what: The wishlist price came from a derived string (priceLabel = price plus ' EUR' in the model), so it was not localised and the generated numeric column showed a number without currency. The shared Price component cannot be placed on a generated table column.
why: No documented way to put the shared Price format on a generated table column; the model string hard-codes the currency.
workaround: Rebuilt the wishlist as a custom view page using Price (see the F41 built item).
note: Same root as c04-06: no way to give a generated numeric column a currency or the shared Price component (GAPS R12-3). Merge into c04-06.

what: Builder claims there is no documented way to read brand values from a runtime settings row; palette and logo are fixed at start-up.
why: Builder's reading of theming.md, which says brand colours belong to model attributes; the catalog does not state whether runtime branding is possible.
workaround: Decision recorded (see F51 decision).
note: theming.md line 101 says brand colours belong on ActorType attributes, which implies fixed at generation, but never states runtime branding is not supported. Add one line stating that.

what: The builder could not find how to read old and new values in the update interceptor and decompiled the dispatcher jar with javap to learn UpdateInstanceCallPayload, without a kb search.
why: Interceptor payload access is not clear from the interceptor page as the builder read it (unverified); the kb was not searched first.
workaround: Used getInput() and getInstance() from the decompiled class.
note: interceptors.md already shows UpdateInstanceCallPayload (getInstance, getInput) but no example of reading old versus new values. Builder skipped kb search first. Add a short old/new comparison example (verify what the payload exposes).

what: The documented command 'mvn clean test -pl application/integration-test' fails from the project root with 'Could not find the selected project in the reactor', because the module is not in the root reactor. The osgi-ds page says the module is built standalone from its own directory.
why: Catalog command does not match the reactor layout described on the osgi page.
workaround: Ran mvn test from the module directory (later the order-tests module).
note: getting-started lines 574-610 and osgi-ds-descriptor-tests line 75 both give mvn -pl application/integration-test from the root; the session and GAPS R12-5 show this fails because the module is not in the reactor. Change to run mvn from the module directory.

what: The testkit has no generated DAO module: the best-practices example uses a project AppDaoModules class that does not exist in the generated project, so the test failed with 'No implementation for ShopConfigDao was bound'. The builder wrote one @Provides per DAO.
why: Catalog example assumes a project DAO module; the generated project does not provide one and the page does not say how to make one.
workaround: Hand-written WebshopDaoModule over ReferenceInjector.
note: best-practices.md line 310 uses AppDaoModules, a class that does not exist in a generated project. Show a small project module with one @Provides per DAO or mark the class as an example to write.

what: After every generate or build the target/judo-cli.jar is deleted, so judo.sh build -i failed with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root was run. Same gap as S01 item 2 (recurring).
why: build-process says build downloads the jar; generate-root and generate delete it.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root before each CLI call.
note: Same root as c04-17 (jar missing after generate or build, recurring S01 item 2).

what: The generator writes only application_en-US.json; the Hungarian file is built by a project script (make-hu-translations.py) from the English keys, and new keys must be added to its dictionary each round. The catalog does not say how to keep a second locale file current.
why: Catalog i18n page covers switching, not maintaining a second generated-style locale file.
workaround: Project script scripts/make-hu-translations.py, run after each generate.
note: Same fix location as c05-46: say a second locale file is project-maintained and new keys must be added each round.

what: Operation buttons and some fields were rejected by update --add feature with the message feature not placeable here, while the same operations existed as UI elements under their own FQN.
why: Unverified: the chunk shows the CLI rule but not the documented route for placing an operation button. The builder did not kb_search this before trying variants.
workaround: Builder updated the generated button element directly by FQN (label, hiddenBy) and did not place it via --add feature.
note: judo-cli line 75 says --add places a widget into a container; operation buttons are OperationForm inside an ActionGroup, which is the same recipe gap as c05-21.

what: Generated after-changeset for the new columns and tables contained an unresolved context variable, so the builder rewrote the file by hand and replaced the variable with sed.
why: Unclear from chunk whether the generator is expected to leave this for the developer. The builder states the generator writes the file empty and the backfill is hand-written.
workaround: Hand-written changeset; sed substitution of the context value; execute passed and counts checked by psql.
note: The ${CTXV} placeholder came from the builder's own heredoc (session L4783); the generator wrote the file empty. Builder mistake, replaced with sed. No catalog change.

what: The admin quote page showed Requested and Order as editable inputs. The documented read-only options exist only for string fields (textWidget TEXT); date, number and enum fields have no read-only attribute in the catalog.
why: Catalog states read-only for strings only; for other types it points to non-editable mapped or derived members, which the catalog does not show for timestamps.
workaround: Added non-editable copies as mapped members (requestedOn, orderRef, numberText) on Quote and AdminQuoteInfo and labelled them; rebuild succeeded.
note: Same root as c05-41: no read-only option for date, number and enum fields.

what: DAO create on a non-composition two-way relation (customerAccountDao.createPointEntries, createGiftCards) failed with MISSING_REQUIRED_RELATION; only the child DAO create with the back reference works.
why: The kb covers creation through composition parents only; the builder found no note for plain two-way relations.
workaround: pointsEntryDao.create(builder.withCustomer(customer)) and giftCardDao.create(builder.withBuyer(buyer)).
note: Page recommends parent-DAO create for containment only; builder shows non-composition two-way relations fail with MISSING_REQUIRED_RELATION through the parent DAO. Add: for plain two-way relations create through the child DAO with the back reference.

what: A seller who opened the direct page address of another seller's product got the product, its status and an Unpublish button. The access filter hid it from lists only.
why: Derived access filters restrict the generated list queries; a direct identifier GET or update is not filtered. Signed identifiers are not bound to a user.
workaround: SellerOwnershipInterceptor on refresh and update, plus ownership checks inside the custom operations; the page shows a refusal toast and an empty form.
note: derived-access-filtering.md says visibility is enforced by the model but does not say a direct GET/update by identifier bypasses list filters. Add a security warning and a write-guard interceptor pointer (verify with the dispatcher).

what: Rates were returned, but the customer currency switch treated the rate as absent: validOn arrives as a Date object in the generated service, so the string comparison of the day failed.
why: Builder's reading of the generated serializer: dates are turned into Date objects; not documented in the catalog as far as checked.
workaround: Compare calendar days built from the Date object in CurrencySwitch.tsx.
note: Catalog never says generated services deserialize date fields to Date objects (so string compare fails). Based on the builder's reading of generated code only; add with verify.

what: Relation tables inside a view show raw member names (TotalLabel, SellerName) unless every column of that table gets its own label and order; row actions sit behind the generated action group drop-down.
why: Labels set on the target transfer object do not reach a relation table in a view; not documented as far as checked.
workaround: Each relation column labelled and moved to an index via a script (cols function).
note: Builder reports relation tables in a view need labels and order per column; no catalog text on this. Single observation, add with verify.

what: Builder states the generated SDK exposes Price and decimal values as java.lang.Double (for example SubOrder.getTotal returns Optional<Double>), so money must be rounded explicitly in Java.
why: Observed in generated sources; the builder did not find this stated in the type-system guide.
workaround: Money helper (see decision on F65).
note: Generated SDK shows Optional<Double> for decimal and Price values (SalesOrderLineDao in session L4000). type-system-guide does not state it; judo-doc-problems already has a numeric-mapping entry. Add: round money explicitly.

what: Setting textWidget=TEXT on read-only string fields removed their labels in the generated order view (values with an icon, no label). The change was reverted to INPUT; the 'read-only shows as text' requirement is not met.
why: The kb says TEXT means read-only but says nothing about labels; the generated theme styles read-only inputs but the builder found no documented labelled-text route.
workaround: Reverted all 158 fields to INPUT via .scratch/r15-model.py; relied on the generated theme read-only styling.
note: widgets.md line 45 says TEXT=read-only but not that the label is dropped in the generated view. Add that effect; possible generator bug worth a ticket.

what: Customers with a saved browser config keep the old vertical drawer because the layout is stored in localStorage under 'webshop-config', which overrides the new model default.
why: Stored client config wins over the generated default layout; the builder found it by testing and cleared localStorage in the browser.
workaround: Cleared the localStorage key in the test browser; real users are not migrated.
note: No page says generated client layout config in localStorage overrides a changed model default. Add: users with stored config keep the old layout until it is cleared.

what: No documented way to hide the generated 'Check out' dialog action on the cart page, so the old and new checkout both exist.
why: Hiding a generated action needs a hiddenBy boolean in the model; the builder left the model change for the owner.
workaround: Left the generated checkout dialog in place; documented in GAPS R15-3.
note: hiddenBy exists (ui-behaviour.md line 44, ui-authoring-guide line 275) but there is no recipe for hiding a generated action; add one: put a boolean on the owner transfer object and set hiddenBy on the action.

what: The kb gives the Stepper widget (a form layout) as the step-flow answer; no catalog entry covers a multi-step operation flow like checkout.
why: kb_search for 'multi-step wizard stepper checkout flow' matched form widgets only.
workaround: Built a custom component instead of a model Stepper.
note: Stepper is documented as a form layout only; no pattern for a multi-step operation flow like checkout. Add a pattern page (custom visual element inside the cart page).

what: A long single test (several minutes with 3-width screenshots) hit ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED; the overhaul spec was split into two tests with a login each.
why: Access token lifetime is shorter than the test; kb search for token renewal in e2e found only error codes, no renewal guidance.
workaround: Split the spec into two short tests.
note: Only error-handling-guide lists ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED; no e2e guidance. Add: keep tests shorter than the token lifetime or log in per test.

what: The Playwright e2e suite runs against the packaged app on port 8181, so the fast Vite loop does not cover it. Each e2e verification needed a full judo.sh build (about 4.5 min per run).
why: No documented way found to point the e2e suite at the dev server; the kb guidance covered only the dev server for manual checks.
workaround: Ran the full build script in the background (.scratch/r14-rebuild.sh) before each e2e run.
note: e2e README line 24 already says tests run against the backend-served frontend, not the dev server. Add the cost: every e2e check needs a full judo.sh build (about 4.5 minutes).
